summary: Repaired /srv/inventory permissions on node1: created inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, set recursive ownership to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, set dirs to 750 and files to 640 (no access for others). Verified read access works for owner and group members but is denied for unrelated users, and file contents (records.csv, config.json) were preserved unchanged. Completed mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id/uptime/permissions/checksums, triggered a systemd reboot on node1, polled until reconnection, confirmed boot_id changed, and reverified permissions, ownership, and file checksums matched the pre-restart baseline.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory ownership/permissions and confirmed inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group did not exist yet
Created group inventory-readers and user inventorysvc (system account, no login shell)
Set directories to 750 and files to 640 recursively
Verified data files content preserved (records.csv, config.json)
Tested access as owner (read ok), as a member of inventory-readers (read ok), and as an unrelated user (permission denied), then cleaned up the two temporary test accounts
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, directory/file listing, and md5sum of both data files
Triggered a deferred systemd reboot on node1 via systemd-run so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed from bef0e5ec... to 3972bbb0..., proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-restart that ownership, permissions, file checksums, and the inventorysvc user / inventory-readers group all matched the pre-restart baseline

evidence.requirement: Existing data ownership repaired to inventorysvc:inventory-readers with correct restrictive permissions, contents preserved
evidence.summary: Baseline showed /srv/inventory owned by root:root 755 with no inventorysvc/inventory-readers accounts. Created the user/group, then chown -R and chmod (750 dirs / 640 files) applied; contents of records.csv and config.json confirmed intact by direct cat output.

evidence.requirement: Access control validated: owner and group members can read, other users cannot
evidence.summary: sudo -u inventorysvc and sudo -u reader_test (member of inventory-readers) successfully read records.csv (exit 0); sudo -u other_test (no group membership) got 'Permission denied' (exit 1). Temporary test accounts were then removed.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id bef0e5ec-ce32-423b-826a-8a5a90584d3a, uptime, directory/file listing showing correct ownership/permissions, and md5sums of both data files prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: reboot acknowledged and executed
evidence.summary: systemd-run scheduled a deferred `systemctl reboot`, returning the acknowledgement (unit name) before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: changed boot identity proven
evidence.summary: Polling showed the old boot_id persisted briefly, then connection timeouts/resets during the actual reboot window, then a new boot_id 3972bbb0-d9b9-42a3-a298-f7638e7792bd with a later uptime -s timestamp, proving the node restarted.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: post-restart recovery verified (permissions, data, accounts)
evidence.summary: After reconnecting, /srv/inventory still shows inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership, 750/640 permissions, identical md5sums for both data files, and both inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group still present — confirming the repair persisted across restart.
